title: Keystone Habit Playbook — Rosa Santos
content:
Purpose: sketch a compact, actionable habit that moves three personal KPIs forward simultaneously — focus time, feature throughput, and signal clarity. This is a scratchpad, not final. Still testing assumptions.

High-level idea:
- Pick 1 keystone habit per month. Small, measurable, repeatable.
- Habit should produce a measurable artifact: reviewed PR, shipped doc, distilled metric insight.
- Combine habit w/ two micro-routines: morning alignment (5m) + end-of-day capture (7m).

Current month (March) keystone: "Focused Code + Context Window"
Why this one? Too many interruptions; large features stall. Hypothesis: 45m uninterrupted dev blocks + 10m structured context capture at EOD will increase merged PRs and reduce rework.

Primary signals (what I’ll measure):
- Signal A: number of merged PRs per week where I am the author (target: +1/week vs baseline).
- Signal B: % PRs merged without >1 revision requested (quality proxy).
- Signal C: Daily uninterrupted focus blocks completed (goal: 5/7 days).
- Signal D: End-of-day context notes created (binary: yes/no).

Baseline (Feb):
- avg merged PRs/week = 1.2
- % single-pass merges = 28%
- avg focus blocks/day = 2.1
- EOD notes capture = sporadic (~2x/wk)

Micro-experiments (2-week cycles):
1) Week 1–2: calendar-guard + 45m timer (pomodoro-lite). Add Slack auto-DND during blocks. Measure adherence.
2) Week 3–4: add pre-block contextual checklist (3 bullets: goal, risks, expected output). See if fewer revision requests.
3) Week 5: pair-review night — 20m buddy review for high-risk PRs. Check merge speed.

Failure modes to watch:
- Over-scheduling blocks that then get interrupted — need gated cancel policy (only cancel for pre-approved high-priority interrupts).
- Capturing context becomes another doc debt item and not helpful — need strict two-line max capture.
- Metrics noisy due to cross-team dependencies — annotate PRs with blockers so I can filter.

Quick templates (for EOD capture):
- 2-line recap: "What I shipped / Why it matters"
- Open questions: 1–2 bullets
- Next mini-step: single todo

Weekly check-in format (Sundays):
- 1) Wins (1–3 lines)
- 2) Misses (why?)
- 3) Metric snapshot (PRs merged, single-pass rate, blocks hit)
- 4) One commitment for next week (specific: e.g., 3 documented reviews)

Sample week (observations):
- Week A: completed focus blocks 4/7, merged PRs 2, single-pass 33% — small improvement.
- Notes: checklist before blocks reduced rework on one mid-sized feature. EOD notes were the high-leverage artifact for async reviewers.

Action list (next 7 days):
- Implement calendar templates with 45m protected blocks (template name: "Keystone Dev") — TODO: add to Google Calendar.
- Share simple checklist in #eng-personal-habits thread for accountability.
- Tag next three PRs with "keystone" label for measurement.

Open questions / hypotheses to test:
- Does a 45m block outperform two 25m blocks for deep design tasks? A/B test across 2 weeks.
- Is a 2-line EOD note enough context for reviewers to avoid re-review? Measure via reviewer comments.

Notes to self (informal):
- When tempted to pack many meetings, protect a single 90–120m weekly deep work slot for architecture.
- Pair review is high friction but high ROI for complex diffs. Try a 20m async + 20m live model.

Slack reminders / accountability: set 3 weekly nudges: Mon AM (commit), Wed midday (check), Fri EOD (capture).

Quick log (recent):
- 2026-03-02: tried 45m blocks, got 3 blocks, low interruptions, shipped v0 of search ranking tweak.
- 2026-03-06: EOD notes missing 2/5 days — need stricter capture time (right after final blocker).

Longer-term stretch goals (quarterly):
- Raise single-pass merge rate to 55%
- Avg merged PRs/week to 2.5
- Reduce average reviewer cycle time by 30% (via better context + labels)

If this is working, package the minimal playbook for teammates: one-pager + calendar template + 3-line checklist. Keep it simple — adoption wins over exhaustiveness.

References / links to tools I use:
- Tiny habit tracker: (Google Sheet) — quick row per day, binary columns for blocks and EOD note.
- Labeling convention: add comment "keystone: context captured" on PR when done.

End of scratchpad. Keep this doc as source-of-truth for experiments; copy the weekly check-ins into a recurring note (weekly-checks tab) so I can chart progress.
